decisions.summary: Adopt sink-type-aware prepend (USB=600ms, HDMI/DisplayPort=1500ms, Bluetooth=1000ms, unknown=1500ms) over the PLAYER_IDLE_TIMEOUT bump alternative.

Probe sink kind from a single `pactl list sinks` (long-form) call that also yields the existing state, replacing the current short-form probe. Parse Driver/Description/device.bus/device.class/api.bluez5 keys to classify; fall back to 'unknown' on any parse error.
On cold start (sink SUSPENDED), prepend silence based on detected sink kind; on warm pw-play reuse, retain the existing 50ms safety prepend with no probe overhead.

Unit tests live alongside the daemon at sync-sources/skills/pan-tts/tests/test_tts_daemon.py, use stdlib unittest.mock (no new dependency), and are run with `python -m unittest discover sync-sources/skills/pan-tts/tests`.
Edit sync-sources/skills/pan-tts/scripts/tts_daemon.py only — .claude/skills/pan-tts/scripts/tts_daemon.py is a sync mirror handled by `pan sync` and must not be edited directly.
Replace the PAN-1028 inline comment block (currently citing 600ms vs 1.5s) with a short reference to the kind→prepend table; keep the implementation self-documenting via a SINK_PREPEND_SECS constant.

hazards.summary: pactl output format varies across PipeWire/PulseAudio versions; Driver/Description strings are not stable enough alone for sink classification.
hazards.mitigation: Classify with a layered match — Driver substring (e.g. 'module-bluez5-device', 'module-alsa-card'), then Properties (device.bus=usb, device.class, api.bluez5.transport), then Description keywords ('HDMI', 'DisplayPort', 'USB'). Treat any unrecognised pattern as 'unknown' so the 1500ms safe default applies.

hazards.summary: `pactl list sinks` is slower than `pactl list short sinks`; calling it on every utterance would regress warm-path latency.
hazards.mitigation: Only probe when spawning a fresh pw-play subprocess (existing `created` flag). Warm-path stays at 50ms with no pactl call. Keep the 2.0s subprocess timeout.

hazards.summary: DisplayPort sinks present as HDMI to ALSA — Description may say either 'HDMI' or 'DisplayPort' or only show the codec name.
hazards.mitigation: Treat the HDMI sink-kind bucket as covering DisplayPort too. Detection MUST match on Driver=module-alsa-card AND (Description contains HDMI/DisplayPort/DP OR device.class=sound and alsa.long_card_name contains GPU vendor). Cover this in unit tests with at least one DisplayPort-shaped pactl fixture.

hazards.summary: Tests run under CI or workspace containers where `pactl` is absent — the production fallback path must not depend on pactl being installed.
hazards.mitigation: Wrap subprocess.run in the existing try/except; on FileNotFoundError or non-zero return, return (state='SUSPENDED', kind='unknown') so the safe 1500ms default applies. Unit tests mock subprocess.run entirely; do not invoke the real pactl.

hazards.summary: Bluetooth latency varies wildly by codec/profile (A2DP-SBC vs LDAC vs HFP); 1000ms is the issue-specified default but may be insufficient for some headsets.
hazards.mitigation: Use the issue-specified 1000ms in this fix. If real-world Bluetooth regressions surface, open a follow-up issue to lift Bluetooth into the 'unknown'/safe bucket (1500ms). Note this trade-off in SKILL.md.

hazards.summary: Two copies of tts_daemon.py exist in the worktree: sync-sources/skills/pan-tts/scripts/ (source) and .claude/skills/pan-tts/scripts/ (sync mirror).
hazards.mitigation: Work agent must edit only sync-sources/. After implementation, run `pan sync` (or commit only sync-sources and let the host-side sync hook propagate) so the mirror stays consistent. Verify the mirror is unchanged-or-resynced before `pan done`.
